text:
As far as I know, you’re in Hadera like we are. I have to say that our recent A/5 extension last November (entering third year) was (surprisingly !) extremely smooth and took less than 20 minutes on the spot — so there’s a very good chance you’ll be able to complete everything during your appointment. Of course, nothing is guaranteed — just sharing our experience as a family with an Israeli kid.

Traveling with the baby to Russia — it doesn’t matter whether you’re traveling together or it’s just the mother — nothing additional is required on the Israeli side, neither when leaving nor when returning. The baby only needs his Israeli passport.
As for the Russian side — I’d recommend having the baby’s birth certificate with the passport. It’s not a mandatory requirement, but they may ask for it.
